notes: Complete project receipts; secured cleanup costs; local benefits delivered; understandable public returns; conflicts disclosed.

DCCEEW’s 30 October 2026 update reports that around three-quarters of Australian gas production is exported. Legislation for the reservation scheme has been introduced to Parliament. The department describes commencement in early 2027, with the principal legislation and licensing framework to commence by proclamation no later than 1 July 2027; supply obligations are planned from 1 January 2028. The proposed domestic supply obligation is up to 20% of annual LNG export volumes, with adjustment mechanisms. Exposure-draft consultation closed on 24 September 2026; current rules remain until new arrangements are implemented. This status was checked on 2 November 2026.

Ask your representatives for a project-level receipt and the assumptions behind any claimed bill reduction. Use published gas consultation outcomes and later instruments to follow implementation; the September submission window is closed.

notes: Australia has a wide range of treaty relationships. The earlier research sketch recorded a historical figure of 2,920 entries (1,669 bilateral and 1,251 multilateral) at the end of 1999; this figure has not been verified against a primary source in this review and is not a current treaty count. This map groups topics so a person can find a thread to pull.

DFAT’s Australian Treaties Database records treaties Australia has signed or on which it has taken other treaty action, with texts and relevant National Interest Analyses. A database entry does not by itself establish that a treaty is currently in force for Australia: check the individual instrument and action history. The earlier 1999 count remains unverified here. Database scope checked 2 November 2026; individual treaty statuses have not all been rechecked. Everything on this page is exploratory, open to correction, and neither legal advice nor adopted policy.
